summary: Frontend-only test of the HID scanner guard (hidGuard.ts) on the web preview at 390x844 mobile viewport. Logged in as pharmacy 07700000001/pass123, tested Buy screen fields (name, barcode, quantity, purchase-price, price, expiry) and Sell screen (autocomplete + credit-modal cust-phone). Rapid bursts (~8ms/key) with Playwright keyboard.type simulate HID scanner speed; 250-300ms delays simulate human typing. 7 of 8 core scenarios pass. ONE REAL FAILURE: on the Sell credit-modal cust-phone input the first digit of a burst LEAKS into the field (result: '8' remained after burst '87654321'+Enter). Root cause: while creditModalOpen=true, useExternalScanner is disabled via the `!creditModalOpen` gate, so the web document-level burst interceptor is unregistered; only hidGuard.useHidGuardedChange remains. That hook's burst check requires (dtLocal<60ms OR dtGlobal<60ms OR hidBuffer.length>0) — the FIRST keystroke of a burst after long idle satisfies none of those, so it commits via setValue before the fast-follow digits are detected. This bug also applies to Android/iOS native fields universally because the doc-level guard is web-only — the same first-digit leak will happen for every field on native (which is exactly the platform the user is complaining about). All Buy-screen tests passed because externalScanner (web doc-listener) is active there and pre-empts before onChangeText fires; the guarded onChangeText behavior alone is NOT sufficient. Also found: conditional React Hook call in buy.tsx Field component (`const guarded = isBarcode ? null : useHidGuardedChange(...)`) violates the Rules of Hooks — safe today because isBarcode is stable per mount but brittle. No red-screen errors, no crashes.

ui_bugs.issue: First digit of a fast HID burst leaks into the phone field (observed: '8' remained after typing 87654321+Enter at 8ms/key). Barcode sent to backend is truncated (missing first digit).

First-digit leak: the burst-detection predicate needs a prior fast key OR non-empty hidBuffer to trigger. The very first key of a fresh burst always slips through setValue. On Android/iOS there is no web document-level fallback, so EVERY field on native will leak the first digit of every scan into the focused input. This defeats the requirement that digits NEVER appear in price/quantity/name/etc.

integration_issues.issue: useExternalScanner is gated by `!creditModalOpen`, disabling the web-only doc-level interceptor while the modal is open. On web this exposes the hidGuard first-digit-leak. Consider keeping externalScanner registered while the modal is open (barcode should still route through handleBarcode); the modal should not exit the scanner subscription.

react_native_issues.issue: Conditional hook call: `const guarded = isBarcode ? null : useHidGuardedChange(value, onChange);` (line 229) violates Rules of Hooks. Works today because isBarcode is stable per mount, but the eslint-disable is a smell. Refactor to always call the hook and conditionally use the returned handlers, or split into two Field components (BarcodeField vs GuardedField). Reference: /app/frontend/app/buy.tsx:229

action_items: Fix first-digit leak in useHidGuardedChange: adopt the same delayed-commit pattern used in externalScanner.tsx web path — when a digit is typed into a non-barcode field, DEFER the setValue call by ~40ms; if a second digit arrives within that window, treat both as burst (revert) and stream into hidBuffer; if no follow-up arrives, commit the single char (human typing).

Do NOT disable useExternalScanner while the credit modal is open (sell.tsx line 66-68). Keep the doc-level interception ALWAYS ON while on Sell/Buy so bursts into modal inputs are intercepted before they touch onChangeText. The modal fields are still routed via handleBarcode → addToCart, so it is safe.
Refactor buy.tsx Field to remove the conditional useHidGuardedChange call (line 229). Either always call the hook or use two component variants.

Native (Android/iOS) has no doc-level guard. Consider adding a globally-mounted invisible always-focused TextInput on Sell/Buy screens (already exists in ExternalScannerProvider on native) to STEAL focus after each keystroke so HID bursts route only there — currently the hidden input only autoFocuses when activeCount>0 and it does NOT re-steal focus from other inputs. This is the more robust native fix.
Retest after fix: repeat TEST 7 (credit-modal cust-phone burst) and confirm result value is EMPTY.
critical_code_review_comments: hidGuard.ts burst detection is asymmetric: it requires timing evidence BEFORE the first key. Use the web pattern (defer + resolve on next-key) to catch first-digit bursts.

sell.tsx line 66-68: gating useExternalScanner on !creditModalOpen creates a scanner-off window where hidGuard alone must protect the modal inputs — and hidGuard is not strong enough on the first key. Remove the creditModalOpen from the enabled gate.
buy.tsx line 229: conditional hook usage; move `useHidGuardedChange` above the conditional or split components.

externalScanner.tsx hidden native input steals focus only on mount (autoFocus) and after emit; when the user taps a real TextInput on Android, focus moves away and never returns until after a full scan flush. A digit typed into that focused TextInput before the burst is detected will leak (same first-digit issue).
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing pharmacy account 07700000001 with existing medicines in stock (Ibuprofen 200 visible).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reproduce TEST 7 as follows: login pharmacy 07700000001/pass123, /sell, search for any letter (e.g. 'ب'), click first ac-hit-* result to add to cart, click pay-credit, focus cust-phone, then simulate rapid keys: `page.keyboard.type('12345678', delay=8)` then `page.keyboard.press('Enter')`. Read `page.input_value('[data-testid="cust-phone"]')` — currently it returns '1' (leak). After fix it should return ''. Also verify /api/medicines/barcode/12345678 (full string, not '2345678') is called. Also add a NATIVE-parity check: temporarily disable externalScanner and confirm the Buy tests also start leaking the first digit — this validates the parallel fix path for Android.
rca_of_issue: hidGuard.useHidGuardedChange's isBurst predicate = (dtLocal<60ms || dtGlobal<60ms || hidBuffer.length>0) && allDigits. On the very first keystroke of a fresh burst: dtLocal=now-0=huge, dtGlobal=now-lastKeyAt (huge if idle >60ms), hidBuffer=''. Predicate is false → setValue(next) commits the char to state. Subsequent keys arrive fast so dtLocal<60ms → burst → reverted. Net effect: exactly 1 leaked character per burst. On Buy screen this is masked by externalScanner.tsx's document-level keydown capture-phase listener which preventDefault's the first digit before onChangeText fires. On Sell credit-modal, externalScanner is DISABLED (enabled: !creditModalOpen), so hidGuard is unshielded and the leak surfaces. On native Android/iOS, externalScanner has NO doc-level capture, so hidGuard is ALWAYS unshielded and the leak affects every field. Mitigation: implement the same delayed-commit pattern inside hidGuard (setValue via setTimeout ~40ms; if a second onChangeText arrives inside the window and both keys are digits, cancel the deferred commit, revert value, feed both chars into hidBuffer).
